assessments.summary: The argument correctly proves that any nonidentity Euclidean rotation preserving a finite noncollinear subset of Z^2 must be a half-turn or quarter-turn. It then correctly uses orbit cardinalities and the no-three-in-line condition to exclude all nontrivial rotations for size 153, and to show that any rotationally symmetric size-154 set must be invariant under the half-turn centered at (38,38), with that center unselected. The declared reference is provenance-only because all necessary orbit and occupancy arguments are reproduced in the subject.
scopeQualifications: The result classifies rotations only, not reflections, affine maps, or approximate symmetries.
The size-154 conclusion is conditional and does not construct such a configuration.
The proof establishes neither existence nor global nonexistence of 153- or 154-point no-three-in-line sets.
It does not identify the rct4 subclass with the full centered half-turn class.
It does not improve the certified bound 152 <= D(77) <= 154.
